chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Howard Scott leaves music for a day job
summary: Scott drank heavily, took a day job as gig work slackened, and played society-type bands after Fletcher.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Well, I had thought about that, and I also thought, you know, I might -- I dare say --
Howard Scott? I don't think Scotty's too much older than me. I don't think he could be. I don't know. He might be around 73.
Well, when did he get out of music then?
Howard got out of music -- he'd been -- he wasn't what you call badly sick, but he used to drink pretty heavy one time.
Oh, he became a lushy at --
But he doesn't look like it.

No. But he took good care of himself, and I think after that -- used to do a lot of gig work, you know, gig -- dances', and the work slacked off, Howard -- everybody was -- went and got a day job. So they give you when you're coming through, so most of the guys had been playing with the big bands, we all got day jobs. Then we gigged when the band would gig. So everybody wanted to get a gig. Call up Stanley Dance, see if he's (unintelligible) work tonight. He was working down at the post office, worked in the band. We'd call him, got a gig for tomorrow night. So we'd make it.

A lot of times a guy wouldn't have nobody else (unintelligible) but those musicians who was working in the daytime because he dependable could be depended upon they knew they'd work the tending. They tended the bar.

Yeah. Well, but, you know, I know about him what you're saying (unintelligible) I forget who else told me that, whether that was Benny Carter or Dickie Wells, but somebody else told me the same thing, that he was the one that sounded like Joe (unintelligible).
But he never got featured as a soloist much, did he?
No, he didn't, because after he left Fletch, he worked with a lot of groups, bands that played almost like a lot of society music.

Played a lot like them bands I was telling you about, like John C. Smith and Happy Roane Wilhelm. The salary sound, it was good. I mean you get a bunch of one nighters, you could take a whole week sometime.
Well, that really would account for that, and then if you can play pretty, that would be very nice in there.
